headline: Profit falls on volume losses; EBITDA outlook narrowed
summary_short: Post's fiscal third-quarter net sales fell 1.8% y/y to $1,948.0M and net income dropped 41.7% to $63.4M, with GAAP diluted EPS down 27.9% to $1.29 as pet food and value cereal volume declines and the lapping of avian-influenza pricing weighed on results.
summary_long: Net sales fell 1.8% y/y as Post Consumer Brands pet food and value cereal volumes declined and Foodservice/Refrigerated Retail lapped prior-year avian-influenza-driven pricing, only partly offset by the 8th Avenue acquisition. Gross margin compressed to 29.1% of sales from 30.0%; SG&A rose to 16.7% of sales from 15.7%. Operating profit fell 19.3% and net income fell 41.7% on lower profit plus higher interest expense (higher debt balances and rates). Nine-month free cash flow rose 19.3% to $401.5M on lower capex. Post repurchased $198.9M of stock in the quarter ($908.8M nine-month), shrinking shareholders' equity 23.0% y/y. Management narrowed FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $1,560-$1,570M (from $1,550-$1,580M) and reiterated FY2026 capex of $370-$390M.

drivers.explanation: Release attributes the quarter to volume declines in Post Consumer Brands (pet food, value cereal) and the lapping of prior-year avian-influenza-driven pricing in Foodservice and Refrigerated Retail.
Excluding acquisitions/divestitures, sales declined across Post Consumer Brands, Foodservice, and Refrigerated Retail; Weetabix was flat. 8th Avenue contributed $141.8M of inorganic sales.
Margin fell to 29.1% of sales from 30.0% alongside the segment-level volume and pricing declines noted for net sales; no separate cost driver disclosed.
SG&A rose to 16.7% of sales from 15.7% (+$14.0M) while gross profit fell $29.9M, compounding the operating-profit decline; specific SG&A driver not itemized.
Lower operating profit combined with higher interest expense, net ($108.2M vs $88.5M), driven by higher average debt balances, a higher weighted-average rate, and lower interest income.
Nine-month capex fell to $289.8M from $360.5M even as operating cash flow was roughly flat ($691.3M vs $697.0M), lifting free cash flow.
Post repurchased $908.8M of stock over nine months (including $198.9M in the quarter) against $242.1M of nine-month net income, a net equity drawdown.
